openings.claim: Stratify existing aggregate counters: compare persistence at similar load across releases and within releases across load bands to separate release-associated from load-associated explanations.
openings.discriminator: Release effect predicts a shift at comparable load; load effect predicts similar load relationships across releases. Neither pattern defeats the discriminator's usefulness.
openings.probe: Read existing aggregate strata; document missing or confounded comparisons before attribution. Keep raw payloads inside the service boundary.
openings.uncertainty: Counters may conceal request mix; missing comparisons or confounding prevent attribution. No observations establish either cause.

openings.claim: Align queue events and latency spikes: queue-buildup and downstream-stall accounts depend on different queue-first versus downstream-first temporal orderings.
openings.discriminator: Reliable opposite ordering defeats the respective account; unresolved clock error defeats the ordering test itself.
openings.probe: First establish whether synchronized timestamps exist, then bound timing error and inspect ordering read-only, preserving the payload boundary.
openings.uncertainty: Synchronized timestamps are indispensable but availability is unknown. Stop the ordering test if synchronization or clock-error bounds remain unresolved; assume no permission change.

lineage.reason: Retains both cross-release and within-release comparisons and their competing predictions.
Retains temporal competition, indispensable synchronization, and clock-error stopping gate.
Delay injection changes service and violates read-only. Predicted stall-signature resemblance and perturbation transfer are untested; non-reproduction would weaken, not eliminate, the stall account.

decision: Prioritize D1; consider D2 only after its timing prerequisites pass. These are untested synthetic proposals with hypothetical resources and no supplied live access. Every causal conclusion must name a falsifiable alternative; neither opening currently establishes attribution.
